issues.body:
PROVENANCE.md § 'Vendored-copy edit policy' states: 'Policy: the vendored files are not edited. vocab/*.yaml.ld and shapes/*.shapes.ttl are byte-for-byte as of origin SHA 0fe80ea7d858de9f02bd29df29f6e50cdada14a0, so the copy can be verified against the origin repo by a plain diff. That verifiability IS the provenance guarantee, and it holds only while the files stay untouched.' It further records a decision dated 2026-07-26 (bead sq-j3p18, issue #3263, raised in the PR #1005 review) that explicitly REJECTED patching a vendored comment, in favour of reconciling divergence in PROVENANCE.md alone.

This PR does the opposite twice over: it appends a new sig-impl:MlDsa node plus a sig-impl:lattice Family to the vendored vocab/sig-impl.yaml.ld, and it rewrites the upstream header comment (lines 1-2). After this change the copy no longer plain-diffs clean against origin SHA 0fe80ea..., so the sole stated provenance guarantee for the whole vendored tree is gone — and gone silently, because the policy text is left unchanged.

There is also an attribution dimension: PROVENANCE.md describes this vocabulary as the companion ontology to the ISWC 2025 ZKP-SPARQL paper by Jesse Wright, Nigel Shadbolt, Jun Zhao and Rui Zhao. Injecting new security-property verdicts into that graph in-place makes new claims appear under those authors' ontology without any marker separating sparq-authored content from vendored content.
issues.fix_hint: Do not modify the vendored file. Follow the pattern the directory already establishes for sparq-authored additions: put the ML-DSA implementation, the sig-impl:lattice Family and the three Assertions in a sparq-owned extension file alongside secprop-ext.ttl (e.g. sigimpl-ext.ttl or vocab-ext/sig-impl-ext.yaml.ld) under the same sig-impl: namespace, exactly as PROVENANCE.md says secprop-ext.ttl 'is the sparq extension and is ours to edit'. Then record the extension in PROVENANCE.md (§ Vendored-copy edit policy and the sub-vocabulary table), keeping the vendored files at SHA 0fe80ea... untouched. If the maintainer instead wants to fork the vendored copy, that is a separate decision that must rewrite the policy section, drop the byte-for-byte claim, and record the new baseline — it should not be a side effect of an ontology-content PR.
issues.title: Edits a file the directory's own PROVENANCE policy declares byte-for-byte vendored and not editable

issues.body:
The diff changes only the sub-vocabulary table row ('Four signature implementations' -> 'Five signature implementations (BBS+, SD-JWT-VC, ed25519, ECDSA, ML-DSA)'). Every other provenance claim in the same document is left as-is, so the file now asserts two incompatible things:

1. § 'What this is': 'This directory is a verbatim vendored copy of the ontology source from the sparql-zkp-ontologies repository', vendored-from commit 0fe80ea7d858de9f02bd29df29f6e50cdada14a0.
2. § 'Vendored-copy edit policy': vocab/*.yaml.ld are 'byte-for-byte as of origin SHA 0fe80ea...' and 'the vendored files are not edited'.
3. The updated table row, which now describes content that does not exist at that SHA.

A reader (or an auditor doing the plain diff the record invites them to do) will find the vendored tree diverges from the stated SHA with no record of what changed, when, by whom, or under what decision. The provenance record is the load-bearing artefact for a vendored third-party ontology carrying an external paper's attribution; leaving it stating a falsehood is worse than the code change itself.
issues.fix_hint: If the extension-file route in the first issue is taken, revert this table edit and instead add a row/section documenting the sparq-authored extension (what it adds, which bead/issue authorised it, and that the vendored files remain at SHA 0fe80ea...). If the fork route is chosen instead, this file must be updated coherently: drop or qualify the 'verbatim'/'byte-for-byte' claims, add a 'Local modifications' section listing the ML-DSA addition and the header-comment rewrite with the authorising decision and date, and state the new divergence baseline so the copy is still auditable against origin.
issues.title: PROVENANCE.md left self-contradictory: table updated to five implementations, byte-for-byte policy claim untouched

issues.body:
Lines 1-2 change from 'yaml-ld source for the four signature implementations the paper considers at round 1: BBS+, SD-JWT-VC, ed25519, ECDSA' to 'yaml-ld source for the five signature implementations considered here: BBS+, SD-JWT-VC, ed25519, ECDSA, and ML-DSA.'

Two problems. First, 'the paper considers' is deleted, so the file no longer says whose scope this is — the provenance link from this vocabulary to the ISWC 2025 paper is quietly severed at the point where new non-paper content is introduced, which is exactly where it matters most. Second, the 'round 1' framing is removed from the header but survives everywhere else: sig-impl.yaml.ld:182 still reads 'round-1 records ed25519/ECDSA-P256 as the deployed pair', and shapes/sig-impl.shapes.ttl:34 still carries the message 'treat round-1 as static; PQ migrations are tracked elsewhere'. That shape message is now directly at odds with the diff, which adds a PQ migration target into this graph rather than tracking it elsewhere.
issues.fix_hint: Restore the upstream header verbatim and carry the sparq addition in the extension file's own header instead. If ML-DSA genuinely belongs in this graph rather than in a PQ-migration graph, reconcile the 'round-1 is static / PQ migrations tracked elsewhere' statement in shapes/sig-impl.shapes.ttl:34 in the same change and say explicitly which graph now owns PQ migration targets, so the two documents do not disagree.
issues.title: Header-comment rewrite drops the paper attribution and 'round 1' scope, contradicting round-1 language left elsewhere

issues.body:
The assertion's justification claims 'a generic proof adapter can conceal the source signature from a presentation verifier', with prov:wasDerivedFrom = [bibo:nist-fips204-2024] as its sole source. FIPS 204 is the ML-DSA standard; it makes no statement whatsoever about zero-knowledge proof adapters, presentation verifiers, or signature-suite blinding. The citation does not support the claim.

The claim is also substantively weaker than the parallel ones it is modelled on. The ed25519 and ECDSA entries assert the same 'generic PoK adapter' escape hatch for group-based signatures, where proof-of-knowledge-of-signature constructions are established (the ECDSA entry cites Crescent for exactly this). Proving an ML-DSA verification relation inside a generic proof system is a materially different and substantially harder problem — an active research area, not a deployed adapter — so copying the 'partial' verdict and the adapter wording across to a lattice scheme overstates what is achievable. Under this repo's ZK/MPC honesty rules an unqualified feasibility claim on a ZK surface must be caveated as research-grade rather than presented as a property that holds.
issues.fix_hint: Either downgrade the verdict to sig-impl:no with a justification that stops at the observable fact (ML-DSA signatures and public keys have distinctive fixed parameter-set encodings, so the algorithm family is revealed), or keep 'partial' and (a) add a real citation for the adapter claim and (b) caveat it explicitly as research-grade / not-yet-deployed for lattice signatures. Do not leave a feasibility claim whose only cited source is FIPS 204.
issues.title: sig-impl:assert-mldsa-sigtype-leakage makes an unsupported ZK-adapter claim citing only FIPS 204

issues.body:
The rdfs:comment asserts 'No deployed W3C Verifiable Credentials cryptosuite currently binds ML-DSA, so integration remains a migration target rather than a presentation-ready suite.' This is a point-in-time claim about the state of an external standards ecosystem, expressed with a bare 'currently' and no date, and the node's only prov:wasDerivedFrom is bibo:nist-fips204-2024, which says nothing about W3C VC cryptosuites.

PROVENANCE.md § 'Authoring / pipeline notes' records the discipline as 'every claim carries prov:wasDerivedFrom pointing at a bibo:Document'. A dateless 'currently' in a vocabulary is guaranteed to go silently stale — the surrounding entries handle this better, e.g. the SD-JWT-VC PQ-forgery justification says 'PQ-JOSE migration (ML-DSA) is in flight at IETF but not yet deployed in SD-JWT-VC profiles' and cites both FIPS 204 and NIST IR 8547.
issues.fix_hint: Date the claim ('as of 2026-07') and cite a source that actually speaks to VC cryptosuite status (NIST IR 8547 for the migration framing, or a W3C VCWG document/tracker for the binding status), or drop the deployment sentence and keep only what FIPS 204 supports.
issues.title: Uncited, undated deployment claim in the sig-impl:MlDsa comment

issues.body:
shapes/sig-impl.shapes.ttl exists but no Rust test, script, or CI workflow loads it against vocab/*.yaml.ld — PROVENANCE.md itself notes 'These files are data, not Rust source: vendoring them does not change the sparq-trust build (nothing include_str!s them today)', and grepping the workspace confirms only secprop-ext.ttl is include_str!'d (crates/sparq-trust/tests/secprop_ttl.rs). The upstream repo's CI validation was not vendored either.

So the new node's conformance is asserted, not demonstrated. Reviewing it by hand it does appear to satisfy SignatureImplementationShape (en-GB langString label, exactly one sig-impl:Family — sig-impl:lattice, declared in the same graph — a boolean postQuantum, three achieves Assertions, one IRI prov:wasDerivedFrom) and each Assertion satisfies AssertionShape (one sec-prop IRI, a verdict in {yes,no,partial}, one langString justification, one provenance IRI). But a future edit has nothing catching it, and this PR adds content without adding the check.
issues.fix_hint: Out of scope for a fix here, but worth filing: add a feature-gated or dev-only test that expands the yaml-ld sources and validates them against shapes/*.shapes.ttl using the workspace's own SHACL support (sparq-shacl), so the ontology tree is gated the way secprop-ext.ttl is by crates/sparq-trust/tests/secprop_ttl.rs. At minimum, state in the PR description how the added node was validated.
issues.title: Change ships with no validation: nothing in the repo SHACL-checks these vocab files

issues.body: No shape requires full property coverage (SD-JWT-VC, ed25519 and ECDSA each cover only three of the eight sec-prop properties, and only BBS+ records PostQuantumSnooping), so this is not a conformance defect. It is however a content gap at the one place the property is most informative: ML-DSA is the only entry in the graph claiming post-quantum forgery resistance, and the BBS+ entry's PostQuantumSnooping assertion draws the hiding-vs-binding distinction under a CRQC that a reader would most naturally want compared against the PQ migration target.
issues.fix_hint: Consider adding a sig-impl:assert-mldsa-pq-snooping Assertion (with a proper citation) so the PQ row of the implementation-by-property matrix is complete, or leave it out deliberately and note in the class comment that snooping is out of scope for this entry.
issues.title: sig-impl:MlDsa omits a sec-prop:PostQuantumSnooping assertion

verdict.summary:
The PR adds an ML-DSA (FIPS 204) entry to crates/sparq-trust/ontologies/zkp-sparql/vocab/sig-impl.yaml.ld and updates the PROVENANCE.md table from four to five signature implementations. The added node is technically well-formed: it satisfies sig-impl.shapes.ttl (label as en-GB langString, exactly one sig-impl:Family with the newly declared sig-impl:lattice, a boolean postQuantum, >=1 achieves Assertion, >=1 prov:wasDerivedFrom); bibo:nist-fips204-2024 really is declared in vocab/prov-ext.yaml.ld; the verdict polarity is right (sec-prop:PostQuantumForgery is 'post-quantum forgery RESISTANCE', so 'yes' for ML-DSA is correct against BBS+/ECDSA 'no'); naming (MlDsa) and British-English prose match the surrounding entries.

It is nevertheless blocked by the directory's own recorded policy. PROVENANCE.md states verbatim: 'Policy: the vendored files are not edited. vocab/*.yaml.ld and shapes/*.shapes.ttl are byte-for-byte as of origin SHA 0fe80ea7d858de9f02bd29df29f6e50cdada14a0, so the copy can be verified against the origin repo by a plain diff. That verifiability IS the provenance guarantee, and it holds only while the files stay untouched.' A decision recorded 2026-07-26 (bead sq-j3p18, issue #3263, PR #1005 review) explicitly REJECTED patching a vendored comment for exactly this reason. This PR both adds content to a vendored file and rewrites its upstream header comment, destroying that guarantee, and it leaves PROVENANCE.md internally contradictory (table says five; the policy section still claims byte-for-byte at that SHA).

Separately, the sig-type-leakage assertion cites only FIPS 204 for a ZK-adapter claim FIPS 204 does not make, and the class comment makes an undated, uncited deployment claim about W3C VC cryptosuites, against the stated 'every claim carries prov:wasDerivedFrom' discipline. Nothing in CI SHACL-validates these files, so the addition ships unverified.
